logic.note: WS2812B protocol decoded from the pin's edges: 24 bits per LED in GRB order, MSB first, the first LED takes the first 24 bits and passes the rest on, a LOW of ≥ 50 µs latches. LEDs that received no new data keep their colour.

timing.note: Pulse widths are measured on the MCU clock to the cycle; a HIGH ≤ 0.6 µs is a 0, longer a 1. Bits outside the datasheet windows (0: 0.22–0.55 µs, 1: 0.58–1.0 µs, the WS2812B and WS2812B-V5 datasheets together) are still decoded and reported, since real LEDs often accept them; newer WS2812B parts need a ≥ 280 µs reset, here 50 µs is enough.

analog.note: Colours are shown as hue × brightness (8 bit per channel, no gamma, no colour temperature). The data input's HIGH threshold (0.7 × VCC = 3.5 V at 5 V, which 3.3 V boards miss) is not checked.

power.note: 1 mA per LED idle plus 20 mA per channel at full brightness (60 mA white) on 5V; warns above 400 mA. No voltage drop along a long strip.

emulates: Bit-exact WS2812B data decoding from firmware
Chained LEDs, partial updates and latching
Supply current for the colours shown
doesNotEmulate: 3.3 V data into a 5 V strip (often fails on hardware: use a level shifter or run the first LED at 4.5 V)
Voltage drop and colour shift along a long strip
testOnRealDevice: Data level from a 3.3 V board
Power: a separate 5 V supply and a 1000 µF capacitor across it for more than a few LEDs
